topic: What a black hole is and how it forms
title: What is a black hole? 🕳️
hook: What is a black hole, and why can't anything escape it?

scenes.narration: What is a black hole, and why can't anything escape it?
Many are born from a giant star, many times more massive than our Sun.
When it runs out of fuel, its core collapses in on itself and the star explodes as a supernova.
What's left is so compact that it has a boundary called the event horizon.
Past that boundary, its gravity is so strong that not even light can escape. That's why it's black.
It's as if it bends space around it, like a heavy ball sinking into a trampoline.
If you fell into a small one, gravity would pull harder on your feet than your head and stretch you like spaghetti.
In twenty nineteen, scientists captured the first image of one: a ring of light around a shadow.
And if you could squeeze the Sun into a black hole, it would be about six kilometers wide, and Earth would keep orbiting it!
Send this to someone who loves space.

claims.statement: Stellar-mass black holes form when the core of a very massive star collapses after it runs out of fuel.
Inside the event horizon gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.
In 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of a black hole (M87*).
The Sun's Schwarzschild radius is about 3 km (≈6 km across); Earth's orbit wouldn't change because the mass would be the same.
